newsitem.title: LATVIA: German banks to enter Latvian market -central bank.
newsitem.headline: German banks to enter Latvian market -central bank.

text.p: Latvia's central bank governor Einars Repse told a news conference on Wednesday that at least two German banks were preparing to take the plunge into the Baltic state's turbulent banking market.
"Dresdner bank is considering turning its representative office in Latvia into a branch," Repse told reporters.
"Another German bank is ready to open a branch office in Latvia at the start of next year," he added, but refused to name the bank or provide further details.
"With the situation stabilized and the banking crisis resolved...Latvia can expect a number of commercial banks to enter its market," he said.
Latvia was hit by a crisis last year in its banking sector with the unexpected crash of its largest bank, Banka Baltija.
The crisis put the brakes on growth, stalled the country's economic recovery and sapped confidence in commercial banks.
A similiar crisis broke over Baltic sibling Lithuania late last year.
The only foreign bank which currently has a branch in Latvia is France's Societe Generale.
Germany's Dresdner Bank has the country's only foreign representative office.

Estonia's Hansabank made the first cross-border bank acquisition in thE Baltic states in June when it bought the Deutsche Lettische Bank but the bank is registered as a Latvian bank owned by foreign capital.
